query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature and irradiation-exposed applications, what intervention could improve mechanical performance while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Minor Al additions (≈2 at%) to a W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V refractory high-entropy alloy will form a dense dispersion of coherent, ordered B2 Al-rich nanoprecipitates during high-temperature aging, increasing 1200 °C yield strength by ≥20 % relative to the equiatomic alloy while keeping irradiation-induced swelling and phase stability unchanged up to 5 dpa at 800–1200 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic W10Ta10Mo10Nb10V10 (at%) refractory high-entropy alloy produced by arc melting and homogenized at 1500 °C/24 h, single BCC solid solution, grain size ~50 µm.
generation.intervention: Micro-alloying with 2 at% Al followed by aging at 1200 °C for 24 h to promote in-situ precipitation of coherent B2 (Al-M) nanoprecipitates (M = Nb, Ta).
generation.conditions: Mechanical tests at 1000–1300 °C in vacuum; heavy-ion (5 MeV Fe2+) irradiation to 5 dpa at 800 °C; grain size maintained at 50 ±10 µm.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale (5–20 nm) coherent B2 Al-rich precipitates uniformly distributed within the BCC matrix, number density ≥10^23 m-3, stable up to 1300 °C.
generation.mechanism: 1. Precipitation strengthening via coherency and order hardening impedes dislocation motion at high temperatures. 2. High interfacial stability and low diffusivity in RHEAs suppress precipitate coarsening, retaining strength. 3. Precipitates and sluggish diffusion enhance point-defect recombination, limiting void swelling under irradiation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength at 1200 °C increases from ~450 MPa (baseline) to ≥540 MPa; steady-state creep rate at 1200 °C/150 MPa remains within ±10 % of baseline; irradiation swelling after 5 dpa at 800 °C remains ≤0.5 %, comparable to baseline.
generation.baseline: Same alloy without Al addition, processed and tested identically (single-phase BCC, no precipitates).
generation.boundary: Al content ≤3 at%; aging temperature 1100–1250 °C; total neutron or ion dose ≤10 dpa; grain size 10–100 µm. Outside these ranges, precipitate stability or grain-boundary phase formation may negate benefits.
generation.uncertainty: No direct experimental data yet link Al-induced B2 precipitation to high-temperature or irradiation performance in this specific alloy family; magnitude of strengthening and swelling resistance is estimated from analogous RHEA and Ni-based superalloy behaviors.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloys: (A) baseline WTaMoNbV and (B) WTaMoNbV-2Al. Homogenize both at 1500 °C/24 h, age at 1200 °C/24 h. Characterize precipitate population (TEM, APT). Conduct tensile tests at 1000, 1100, 1200 °C. Irradiate dog-bone samples with 5 MeV Fe2+ ions at 800 °C to 5 dpa. Measure post-irradiation swelling (TEM void density, dilatometry) and nanoindentation hardness.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if (i) yield strength improvement at 1200 °C is <10 %, or (ii) steady-state creep rate increases by >20 %, or (iii) irradiation swelling in alloy B exceeds baseline by >0.2 percentage points, or precipitates coarsen to >50 nm after aging.
